idea_generation.summary: SCALE proposes detecting DBMS performance anomalies via a single-DBMS scaling-law oracle plus distribution mutation, with controlled injected-cliff benchmarks and baseline comparisons. The experiments are already implemented and report high recall and plan attribution. Novelty is incremental relative to existing performance-bug detection and query-aware data generation. The plan gives reproducible commands and success criteria but lacks method-level detail on oracle construction and distribution mutation.
strengths: Concrete success signals with measurable thresholds and achieved results.
Includes controlled injected benchmarks and baseline comparisons against CERT, APOLLO, and HULK.
Plans for plan attribution and false-positive evaluation.
Reproducible environment choices and fixed seeds.
weaknesses: Core method is only summarized as 'single-DBMS scaling-law oracle + distribution mutation' without algorithmic detail.
The provided artifact is only an experiment plan; the referenced idea.md is not included.
Depends on comparing with HULK, but HULK is not fully operational in the environment because it needs a second DBMS.
Generalization beyond three tested DBMSs and three injected cliffs is not established.

original.paper_title: Hulk: Exploring Data-Sensitive Performance Anomalies in DBMSs via Data-Driven Analysis

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: Hulk is a data-driven analysis approach that automatically explores data-sensitive DBMS performance anomalies by synthesizing data-sensitive queries and sampling response-time trends of the target DBMS and a comparable DBMS as data volume increases.
claims.evidence_quote: we propose Hulk to automatically explore these data-sensitive performance anomalies via data-driven analysis.

claims.statement: Data-sensitive performance anomalies arise from implementation errors in CBO components and can cause dramatic response-time fluctuations with small changes in data volume.
claims.evidence_quote: Any implementation errors may cause performance to fluctuate abnormally when the dataset changes.

claims.statement: Hulk reported 135 anomalies on six widely used DBMSs, and 129 were confirmed by developers as new bugs.
claims.evidence_quote: Hulk totally reports 135 anomalies, with 129 have been confirmed as new bugs, including 14 CVEs.

claims.statement: Among the 129 confirmed bugs, 94 are data-sensitive performance anomalies and 35 are crash bugs; 14 were assigned CVE IDs.
claims.evidence_quote: 94 anomalies are data-sensitive performance anomalies, and 35 anomalies cause the DBMS crash.

claims.statement: The detected data-sensitive performance anomalies span CBO components: 41 are CE-related, 13 are CM-related, and 40 are PE-related.
claims.evidence_quote: We can see that 41, 13, and 40 performance anomalies are due to the implementation errors in CE, CM, PE, and others, respectively.

claims.statement: Detected data-sensitive performance anomalies cause serious slowdowns: 42 exhibit 1x-10x degradation, 30 exhibit 11x-20x, 13 exhibit 21x-30x, and 9 exhibit over 30x.
claims.evidence_quote: 42, 30, 13, and 9 anomalies exhibit speed decreases of 1x-10x, 11x-20x, 21x-30x, and over 30x, respectively.

claims.statement: Many Hulk-detected anomalies are realistic: 58 cases could be reproduced with queries containing fewer than 10 clauses, and 74 triggering queries contain no more than 20 clauses.
claims.evidence_quote: 58 cases could be reproduced using queries comprising fewer than 10 clauses and typical workloads after reducing the test cases.

claims.statement: A motivating MySQL anomaly shows that a 0.1% increase in data volume from inserting 10 rows caused response time to rise from 1.75s to 67.43s, a 3753% increase.
claims.evidence_quote: With a 0.1% increase in the amount of data, the response time increases by 3753%.

claims.statement: A motivating Percona anomaly shows that inserting only 5 rows in two tables caused execution time to rise from 0.57s to 13.03s, a 2185% performance degradation.
Hulk found long-hidden bugs, with 21 detected bugs hidden for over 5 years and one imported 9 years ago.
claims.evidence_quote: Besides, 21 of the detected bugs have been hidden in the DBMSs for over 5 years.

claims.statement: SCALE detects injected cost-model performance cliffs with scale_recall true and scale_false_positives 0 in the cm_count, cm_group, and cm_selfjoin benchmark cases.
claims.evidence_quote: Results show SCALE localizes injected cliffs with high recall and few false positives while the baselines either miss them or cannot operate on a single DBMS.

claims.statement: Injected cost-model anomalies caused large execution-time degradations at the cliff volumes: cm_count ratio 1347.8861472122212, cm_group ratio 1008.867743125935, and cm_selfjoin ratio 952.8440821356854.
SCALE detected a data-distribution anomaly in the dist_lowcard case, with max lowcard-over-uniform execution-time ratio of 533.8213739240983 and scale_detected true.
In the cm_group case, APOLLO recalled the injected cliff but produced one false positive.
CERT did not flag the injected cost-model benchmark cases cm_count, cm_group, and cm_selfjoin.

SCALE removes external-reference dependencies by fitting a Theil-Sen regression of response time versus data volume in log-log space on a single DBMS and flags persistent, statistically significant super-linear deviations.
claims.evidence_quote: SCALE fits a robust scaling law (Theil–Sen regression of response time versus data volume in log-log space) on a single DBMS and flags a performance cliff as a persistent, statistically significant super-linear deviation

agent.overall_conclusion: SCALE, evaluated on PostgreSQL 16.2, DuckDB 1.5.5, and SQLite 3.53, detects injected cost-model cliffs at volumes 8,000-16,000 with degradation ratios from 952.8440821356854 to 1347.8861472122212, scale recall true, and zero SCALE false positives for cm_count, cm_group, and cm_selfjoin cases. It also detects a low-cardinality cardinality-estimation anomaly with max ratio 533.8213739240983. Baselines show limitations: APOLLO has one false positive in cm_group, and CERT does not flag the injected cost-model cases.
